p:cNvPr.descr: Image (b) begins with oxaloacetate, where C bonds down and left to -O, ad double bonds up and left to O (all in pink). A red arrow points from the negative sign to the bond line between C and –O. C, also bonds right to CH2, which bonds right to C. A red arrow points from C to the bond line between CH2 and C. The second C also double bonds down to O and bonds right to C, which double bonds up and right to O and bonds down and right to O-. This is added to GTP, where Guanosine in a tan box bonds right to O, which bonds right to P, which double bonds up to O, bonds down to O- and right to O. O bonds right to P, which double bonds up to O, bonds down to O-, and bonds right to O, which bonds right to P. A red arrow points from this bond line back to O. A red arrow also points from the double bond from C down to O in the first molecule to the P just mentioned. This P also double bonds up to O, bonds down to O- and right to O-. Below this is an arrow pointing down to phosphoenolpyruvate. To the left of the arrow is PEP carboxykinase in blue. To the right, another arrow points right to GDP, and another arrow jets off and points to a pink CO2. Phosphoenolpyruvate begins with C, which double bonds left to CH2, bonds right to COO-, and bonds up to O (with a thick bond line), which bonds right to PO2 over 3[negative].
